answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and place them face down; shuffle the nine Conflict II cards and deal five face down on top; shuffle the three Conflict I cards and deal one face down on top. The deck has 10 cards in order: one I, five II, four III. Return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom’; unused cards are returned to the box without looking.

answers.answer: In a four-player game, a human starts at 1 VP; in a three-player game, at 0 VP. In either game, the human has two Agents on their Leader and a third Agent (the Swordmaster) beside the board, three troops in their garrison and nine in supply, and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: Score track is 1 in a 4-player game and otherwise 0; place two Agents on the Leader and the third beside the board; three troops in garrison, remaining nine in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain. Once you Reveal, you skip the rest of the Player Turns phase and cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards still in your hand and revealed on that Reveal turn, not cards played on Agent turns. During Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both kinds of turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: ‘you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents’ and after it your turns are skipped; Reveal Turn resolves just-revealed cards only; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to your discard pile.

answers.answer: No. You must pay the destination cost immediately before resolving any effects of the space or the card, so an Agent-turn card effect cannot first provide resources for that cost. One card can send only one Agent, using one Agent icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn; it can only be revealed on a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs ‘before resolving any effects of the space or the card you played’; choose only one Agent icon and one card cannot send multiple Agents; a card without icons can only be revealed.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, you may deploy all three troops recruited this turn plus up to two from your existing garrison, for up to five total. At a non-Combat space, recruited troops remain in the garrison. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison before deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: recruit a troop from supply into garrison; at a Combat space deploy any or all units recruited that turn plus up to two more from garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any board space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; it does not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to let your Agent enter an opponent-occupied space. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy to draw a card whenever you send an Agent; choose immediately after placing the Agent, before getting effects from the space or played card. The same Spy cannot be recalled for both effects, but different Spies may be used for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on the same placement.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy icon uses a Spy at a connected post without recalling it; Infiltrate ignores an opponent's Agent; Gather Intelligence is chosen after placement and before effects; one Spy cannot be used for both, though two may be used.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops give 4, one sandworm gives 3, and four revealed swords give 4. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. You cannot participate in the Combat Intrigue window without at least one unit in the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Strength: each troop is 2, each sandworm 3, and each revealed sword 1; if your last unit is removed strength becomes 0. Combat Intrigue is for players with at least one unit in the Conflict.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you from acting again later in the phase. The window closes when all players involved in Combat have passed consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not their garrison), and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: ‘not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; resolve after all involved pass consecutively; cleanup returns troops to supply and sandworms to the bank.

answers.answer: In either player count, tied first-place players each take the second reward, and no one wins the Conflict or takes its card. In a three-player game, no other rewards are given. In a four-player game, if exactly two tie for first, the remaining players compete for the third reward; if three or more tie for first, there are no other rewards. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first players each gain the second reward and nobody takes the card; with three or fewer players there are no other rewards, while in four players exactly two tied first leave the third reward for the others. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles the rewards you take; additional sandworms do not multiply them further. Taking control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a doubled reward offering 1 VP for 3 spice, you may pay 3 spice for 1 VP or pay 6 spice to gain 2 VP; the optional cost may be paid a second time for the second instance.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: ‘one or more sandworms’ doubles rewards; control and battle icons cannot be doubled; optional reward cost may be paid a second time (example: 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 spice for 2).

answers.answer: After the winner takes the Conflict card into their supply face up, check for a normal battle-icon match. A matching card may be another face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply; the match is mandatory, and you flip the pair face down to gain 1 VP. During Endgame, the wild icon may match any one of the three battle icons in your supply, also flipping the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: when you win and take the card into your supply, check for another face-up Conflict or Objective card with the same icon; if found, you must flip the pair for 1 VP. Wild matching is during Endgame.

answers.answer: Reaching 2 Influence gains 1 VP; falling below 2 loses it, and reaching 2 again regains it. Reaching 4 gains the printed track bonus; you keep that bonus if Influence later falls below 4 and earn it again on returning to 4. The first player to reach 4 also takes the Alliance token and its 1 VP. Simply tying the current holder at 4 does not steal the Alliance. Under the FAQ clarification, if the holder later loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied player takes it; if the holder falls to 3 or lower, the Alliance is lost and returned to the board if nobody has 4+ Influence to take it.
answers.evidence: Scoring table: VP at 2 and track bonus at 4 have the stated loss/recovery behavior; an opponent rising higher takes the Alliance, while tying does not. FAQ: a formerly tied player takes it if the holder loses Influence; at 3 or lower it returns to board if no one at 4+.

answers.answer: During Reveal, Persuasion can be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources to buy one card or split Persuasion from one source among different cards. After acquiring a Row card, its replacement is available immediately if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: Persuasion may be used before, between, or after Reveal effects. Acquiring Cards: Persuasion may be pooled or split; the Row stays at five and you may acquire a replacement; acquired cards go face up to discard.

answers.answer: At the Makers phase, each Maker space without an Agent gets 1 spice added to its bonus-spice spot; visiting a Maker space lets you take all bonus spice there. While the Shield Wall token remains, no sandworm can be summoned to a Conflict at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin. Maker Hooks are required only when the particular summoning effect specifies them; they are retained and not spent. A sandworm is summoned directly to your Conflict quadrant and can never be put in a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers: Agent-free spaces get 1 bonus spice, and a visitor gains all bonus spice. Sandworms: Hooks are not universal and are never spent; Shield Wall prevents summoning at its three locations; worms immediately deploy to Conflict and can never be in garrison.

answers.answer: At Recall, at the end of a round, 10 or more VP for any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Before comparing scores, players may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue cards. The player with the most VP wins; rulebook tiebreakers, in order, are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Recall checks 10+ VP or an empty Conflict Deck; Scoring says Endgame Intrigue resolves first, then most VP wins, with tiebreakers spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup has two contracts face up on the board and the remaining 18 of the 20 standard contracts face down in the bank. Add four Intrigue cards to the Intrigue Deck and four Imperium cards to the Imperium Deck. Shaddam Corrino IV is an optional Leader, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix compatibility and are left out of standard CHOAM setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: flip two of 20 contracts face up and place 18 face down in bank; add 4 Intrigue and 4 Imperium cards; Shaddam is optional. Contrasting-back 10 are a separate Rise of Ix set, left in the box.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts and replace it with a bank contract flipped face up. If all contracts have been taken, the icon gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract is completed by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the contract's shown amount of spice during that turn in total, including from other sources. The Immediate contract is completed as soon as taken. The Acquire The Spice Must Flow contract is completed when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Taking contracts and Completing contracts sections specify the face-up replacement, 2 Solari fallback, and the Harvest, Immediate, and Acquire completion conditions.

answers.answer: No. If you acquire a contract for a board space after already sending your Agent there that turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must hold the contract when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its listed rewards, then flip the contract face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM completion: a contract for a space already visited that turn must wait until a future turn; you must have held it when sending the Agent. Completion means announce, gain rewards, flip face down, and leave in supply.

answers.answer: Standard two-player play uses one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; the other two eligible Objectives are dealt to the humans, and the human whose Objective shows the First Player marker goes first. First Player alternates only between humans. Each round's order is First Player, Rival, then the other human. The Rival takes Agent turns while an Agent remains in supply and never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: use one shared scoring Rival; give it Ornithopter and deal the other two Objectives to humans; First Player is human and alternates between humans; order is First Player → Rival → other human; Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: When the Rival reveals a destination that is occupied, it ignores that destination and reveals another House Hagal card. A Place Spy card uses an empty observation post of its specified type, or ignores the placement if none is available; either way it reveals another Hagal card because it has not sent an Agent. Rivals ignore ordinary board-space costs and effects and apply only the revealed House Hagal effects. If House Hagal is empty or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle it and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore occupied destinations and reveal again; ignore normal costs/effects and apply Hagal effects only; immediately reshuffle on empty deck or Reshuffle. Spies and Schemes: Place Spy uses an empty specified post or ignores placement, then reveals another card because no Agent was sent.
